cards.title: Initial sort state after a feed loads
cards.body: Today a loaded feed displays items in the order the server returned them. Once the toggle exists, which state is it in — and therefore which order does the list show — immediately after a successful load?

options.text: Newest first — the toggle starts on 'Newest' and the loaded list is sorted by publication date right away
Newest selected but list in feed order — the toggle shows 'Newest' while the display stays in server order until the user toggles
Feed order until the first toggle — the list shows server order until the user picks a direction

rec.why: The toggle is the only control over order, so its displayed state must match what the list shows; a control claiming 'Newest' over feed order (b) would lie, and (c) leaves the toggle's meaning undefined until clicked. Police feeds are usually newest-first anyway, so (a) is typically a no-op on load and only changes the outcome for feeds that arrive out of order — exactly the case this feature targets.

cards.title: Sort state across Load and Refresh
cards.body: loadFeed() already resets the search box on every successful load, and Refresh reloads the currently loaded feed. Does the toggle keep the user's chosen direction across a Refresh or a newly loaded feed, or reset to its default state like the search box?

options.text: Reset to the default direction on every successful load, like the search box
Keep the user's chosen direction across loads within the session

rec.why: The existing rule is that a fresh load shows the feed's full list in a fresh state; carrying a sort direction across loads would silently reorder a feed the user just swapped, and 'Refresh' would then show a different order than the same feed's first load.

cards.title: Items without a parseable publication date
cards.body: The sort key is each item's pubDate. Some feeds omit pubDate or ship a string that cannot be parsed as a date. Where do such items land while 'Newest' or 'Oldest' is active?

options.text: Always last in both directions, keeping their relative feed order among themselves
Treated as the oldest possible time, so they sink to the bottom under 'Newest' and rise to the top under 'Oldest'
Left out of the sorted list entirely

rec.why: An item must not vanish because its date is missing — (c) would hide content the item-count label still counts, breaking the count. (b) puts undated items above dated ones under 'Oldest', which reads as a false claim of recency; pinning them last in both directions keeps them reachable and never above a dated item.

cards.title: Items with identical timestamps
cards.body: When two loaded items carry the same publication date, which order do they display in under 'Newest' and under 'Oldest'?

options.text: Their original feed order in both directions (stable sort)
Feed order under 'Newest', reversed feed order under 'Oldest'

rec.why: A stable sort makes the display predictable and keeps the two directions exact mirrors of each other; ties are common when a feed stamps the same day-level date on several reports, and flipping the toggle then reshuffling those tied items for no visible reason would look like a bug.

cards.title: Open item detail when the direction flips
cards.body: The list renders indices into feedItems and selectedIndex points into that array. When the user flips the toggle while an item's detail (including a possibly still-loading AI summary) is open, what happens to that open detail?

options.text: It stays open and moves with its item to the item's new position
It closes when the direction changes

rec.why: The feature states the open detail keeps working as today: like the search filter today, reordering the displayed indices does not change which item is selected, so closing it would be a regression and would discard an in-flight or completed analysis the user explicitly opened.

cards.title: Shape of the toggle control
cards.body: What control sits next to the feed search box to choose between Newest and Oldest?

options.text: One two-state button showing the current direction ('Newest' or 'Oldest') that flips on click
A segmented pair of buttons, one per direction, with the active one visually marked (aria-pressed)
A dropdown select offering the two directions

rec.why: Both options are visible at once, so the existence of the other order is discoverable without clicking, and the active state is declared rather than inferred; a flipping button (a) changes its own label on every click, and a dropdown (c) hides a two-value choice behind an extra interaction.

cards.title: When the toggle is visible
cards.body: The search box renders only while a feed is loaded and has items (loadedFeed && feedItems.length). When should the sort toggle render?

options.text: Exactly with the search box — same condition, placed next to it
Always visible, disabled while no feed with items is loaded

rec.why: 'Next to the feed search box' pins its place, and with zero loaded items there is nothing to reorder; an always-present but permanently dead control in the empty state adds noise without function.

cards.title: Confirmation of shared understanding
cards.body: The picture after this round: a two-option Newest/Oldest control next to the feed search box, visible whenever the search box is, reorders only the currently loaded feed's already-loaded items client-side by publication date — no refetch. The active search filter keeps filtering and the count label keeps counting; an open detail stays open and follows its item. Undated items sort last in both directions, ties keep feed order, the sort is stable, and every successful load (Load or Refresh) resets the toggle to its default direction. Confirm this as the shared understanding to take into the Spec?

options.text: No — I will correct it in a note

rec.why: This restates exactly what the round's answers pin down; confirming it ends the Grill and lets the Spec be written from a settled picture.
